items.title: Antonelli leads the extended Qatar FP2
items.summary: Kimi Antonelli set 1:23.077, 0.127 seconds ahead of George Russell; Lando Norris was third at +0.445s. The FIA Document 21 table matches Formula1.com across all 22 classified drivers. Two red flags interrupted the session, which was extended by 13 minutes. A Virtual Safety Car followed when Hamilton stopped after reporting lost power.
items.why_it_matters: The official report does not establish a cause for Hamilton's loss of power. The interrupted session is not a long-run comparison.

items.title: FIA fines Audi €500 for Hülkenberg pit-lane speeding
items.summary: Document 20 records Car 27 at 84.4 km/h in the 80 km/h pit lane during FP2. The €500 fine is imposed on Audi Revolut F1 Team, not the driver.
items.why_it_matters: This is a team fine, not a grid penalty or sporting penalty for Hülkenberg.

items.title: FIA publishes Qatar post-FP2 procedure times
items.summary: Document 22 moved Friday’s Drivers’ Meeting to 22:43 local; FP2 cars were due covered and ready for seals by 00:13 Saturday, with Restricted Period Three starting at 01:13. Document 23 sets a 1:41.0 maximum between the Safety Car lines for qualifying and specified race-reconnaissance laps.
items.why_it_matters: These are post-session obligations and a race-control threshold, not changes to the published F1 session timetable.

items.title: Qatar pre-weekend tyre-set totals remain inconsistent
items.summary: Formula1.com’s preview lists 2/3/8 sets with an extra Soft reserved for Q3, while its explainer lists 2/4/7. Pirelli confirms C1/C2/C3 and the 27-lap limit, but neither source resolves the totals or reports remaining sets. The FIA listing refreshed after FP2 through Document 23 contains no later pressure table.
items.why_it_matters: Keep both allocations attributed; use neither as remaining sets or as a race-strategy inventory. The latest pressure values are not a post-FP2 reaffirmation.

items.title: Alonso returns after missing Qatar FP1
items.summary: Formula1.com reports that Fernando Alonso returned in FP2 after missing Thursday media day while recovering from a virus. Jak Crawford drove Alonso’s Aston Martin in FP1.
items.why_it_matters: Crawford’s FP1 appearance was a practice substitution, not a change to the race line-up.
